questions.question: Why did Tricki become ill?
questions.model_answer: Tricki became ill because he was overfed and given too little exercise. Mrs Pumphrey pampered him with rich food and treats, so he became overweight, lethargic and unhealthy.

questions.question: How did Herriot cure Tricki without medicine?
questions.model_answer: Herriot took Tricki to his surgery and controlled his diet. Tricki was given simple food and plenty of exercise by playing with the other dogs. Within a short time he became active and healthy again. The story shows the value of discipline and exercise.

questions.question: Why is the title A Triumph of Surgery humorous?
questions.model_answer: There is no complicated surgery involved in Tricki's recovery. Herriot simply removes him from excessive food, gives him exercise and allows him to socialise with other dogs. The title humorously presents ordinary care and discipline as a great medical triumph.

questions.question: What name did the thief use when he met Anil?
questions.model_answer: He introduced himself as Hari Singh.

questions.question: Why did Hari Singh return the stolen money?
questions.model_answer: Hari Singh realised that Anil's trust and kindness gave him a chance to become educated and change his life. His conscience made him return the money rather than lose that opportunity.

questions.question: How did Anil's behaviour change Hari Singh?
questions.model_answer: Anil trusted Hari Singh even though he knew little about his past. He offered him food, shelter and promised to teach him to read and write. This kindness awakened Hari's conscience. He began to value education and an honest future more than the money he had stolen.

questions.question: How was Ausable different from the secret agent Max expected?
questions.model_answer: Ausable was fat and ordinary-looking rather than physically impressive. However, he was extremely intelligent and calm. He defeated Max through quick thinking rather than physical strength.

questions.question: How did Ausable get rid of Max?
questions.model_answer: Ausable invented a story about a balcony outside his room and then pretended that the police were coming. When there was a knock, Max believed Ausable's explanation and jumped towards the supposed balcony to escape. In reality there was no balcony, so Max fell.

questions.question: How does The Midnight Visitor show that intelligence is more important than appearance?
questions.model_answer: Ausable does not look like the stereotypical secret agent. He is overweight and unimpressive, while Max appears threatening with a pistol. Yet Ausable remains calm and uses clever deception to defeat Max. His invented balcony and police story turn Max's confidence against him. The story shows that intelligence and presence of mind can overcome physical strength.

questions.question: What was Horace Danby's unusual hobby?
questions.model_answer: Horace Danby collected rare and expensive books.

questions.question: How was Horace Danby deceived?
questions.model_answer: A young woman pretending to be the owner of the house convinced Horace that she had forgotten the safe combination. She persuaded him to open the safe for her. Horace did so and was later arrested because his fingerprints were left at the scene.

questions.question: Explain the irony in Horace Danby's situation.
questions.model_answer: Horace carefully planned his burglaries and considered himself respectable in ordinary life. Yet another thief tricked him into opening the safe for her. Horace left his fingerprints and was arrested, while the woman escaped with the jewels. The criminal who believed he was clever became the victim of a cleverer criminal.

questions.question: Why was Griffin invisible?
questions.model_answer: Griffin had discovered a scientific method that made the human body transparent and therefore invisible.

questions.question: Why can Griffin not be called a responsible scientist?
questions.model_answer: Griffin uses his scientific discovery for selfish and criminal purposes. He steals clothes, money and food and commits acts of violence. Instead of using science for human welfare, he uses it to satisfy his own needs.

questions.question: What warning does the story give about the misuse of science?
questions.model_answer: The story shows that scientific knowledge without moral responsibility can become dangerous. Griffin's invisibility is a remarkable achievement, but he uses it for theft, violence and personal gain. The story therefore suggests that scientific power must be guided by ethics and responsibility.

questions.question: How did Richard Ebright's mother contribute to his success?
questions.model_answer: Ebright's mother encouraged his curiosity, provided books and materials, and involved him in useful activities. She helped him develop disciplined study habits and supported his scientific interests from childhood.

questions.question: What helped Ebright become a successful scientist?
questions.model_answer: Ebright's success came from curiosity, hard work, disciplined observation and his mother's encouragement. He learned from experiments, entered science fairs and gradually developed more advanced research. He also remained focused and competitive without giving up after setbacks.

questions.question: What qualities of Richard Ebright can students learn from?
questions.model_answer: Students can learn curiosity, perseverance, careful observation, disciplined work and the willingness to learn from failure. Ebright did not depend only on talent; he worked systematically, read widely and tested ideas through experiments. His mother's guidance also taught him the importance of sustained effort.

questions.question: Why was Matilda unhappy with her life?
questions.model_answer: Matilda was dissatisfied because she dreamed of wealth, luxury and social status. Although she lived comfortably enough, she constantly compared her life with the rich lifestyle she imagined she deserved.

questions.question: What is ironic about the necklace in The Necklace?
questions.model_answer: Matilda and her husband spend ten years repaying a huge debt after losing the necklace. They finally learn that the original necklace was only an imitation worth very little. Their suffering was therefore caused by a false assumption about the necklace's value.

questions.question: How does The Necklace teach a lesson about appearance and contentment?
questions.model_answer: Matilda's desire to appear wealthy makes her borrow a necklace and enjoy one evening of luxury. When it is lost, she and her husband sacrifice ten years of their lives to replace it. The final revelation that the necklace was false exposes the cost of vanity and dissatisfaction. The story encourages honesty, contentment and freedom from excessive concern about social appearance.

questions.question: How did education change Bholi?
questions.model_answer: Education gave Bholi confidence and self-respect. Her teacher encouraged her to speak and learn without fear. As she grew confident, she was able to reject an unfair marriage proposal and choose dignity over social pressure.

questions.question: Why did Bholi refuse to marry Bishamber?
questions.model_answer: Bishamber demanded dowry and insulted Bholi by treating her appearance as a defect. Bholi realised that such a man did not deserve her respect or trust. Education had made her confident enough to reject the proposal and protect her dignity.

questions.question: Explain how Bholi's teacher becomes an agent of transformation.
questions.model_answer: Bholi's teacher treats her with patience and affection when others consider her weak and unattractive. The teacher encourages her to speak, learn and believe in herself. Education gradually replaces Bholi's fear with confidence. This transformation enables her to challenge an unfair marriage arrangement and become an independent, self-respecting person.

questions.chapter: The Book That Saved the Earth
questions.question: What did Think-Tank believe the nursery rhyme book was?
questions.model_answer: Think-Tank believed the book was a source of highly advanced information and misunderstood its nursery rhymes as serious messages.

questions.chapter: The Book That Saved the Earth
questions.question: Why is Think-Tank's interpretation of the book humorous?
questions.model_answer: Think-Tank lacks common sense and interprets simple nursery rhymes as secret military messages. His exaggerated conclusions make ordinary lines about familiar objects seem like threats to an entire alien civilisation.

questions.chapter: The Book That Saved the Earth
questions.question: How does The Book That Saved the Earth use misunderstanding to create humour?
questions.model_answer: The Martians misunderstand a simple book of nursery rhymes and believe its contents reveal Earth's military power. Think-Tank makes increasingly absurd interpretations and finally orders the invasion to be cancelled. The gap between the simple meaning of the rhymes and the Martians' frightening interpretation creates the comedy.
